n5-en: A stray coin rolls into a <radical>wide box</radical> with no lid. It spins in loops all night and rubs its edges perfectly smooth. By morning it is a shiny <kanji>circle</kanji> of yen.
n5-furui: A <radical>mouth</radical> counts slowly to <radical>ten</radical> every single morning. It has counted so many mornings that the counting itself feels ancient. Something repeated this many times can only be <kanji>old</kanji>.
n5-go-language: A waterfall of <radical>speech</radical> pours down into a waiting <radical>mouth</radical> below. The mouth swallows every word whole without chewing once. Stuffed with so many words, it finally speaks a whole <kanji>language</kanji>.
n5-hana: A tuft of <radical>grass</radical> gets tired of being trampled every day. It shoots one blade straight up and pops a bright bloom on top. Now people step around it, admiring the new <kanji>flower</kanji>.
n5-hyaku: A single <radical>one</radical> stroke sits on top of a blinding <radical>white</radical> light bulb. The light is so bright the stroke multiplies into copies of itself. Soon there are exactly a <kanji>hundred</kanji> strokes glowing on the ceiling.
n5-kawa: Three thin <radical>river</radical> lines trickle down a mountainside side by side. A storm swells all three until they touch and merge together. Merged into one, they roar as a single wide <kanji>river</kanji>.
n5-machi: A farmer paces around his single square <radical>rice field</radical> every single day. Slowly other families build houses right along its edges. Soon a whole <kanji>town</kanji> surrounds that one small field.
n5-man: A single banner flaps above a busy market stall. The vendor scrawls one more zero on it every time a customer buys something. By nightfall the banner is crammed with exactly <kanji>ten thousand</kanji> zeros.
